_comment: Research-coverage config. We walk the FILESYSTEM (not just git) so untracked files count too. 'Coverage' = every non-excluded file has a current-hash research entry in the ledger. Excludes are declared so coverage is honest: we cover everything except these vendored/derived paths.
_enumeration: Files = git-tracked ∪ git-untracked-not-ignored. This honors .gitignore (skips build caches, uploads, node_modules, _build) yet still covers untracked SOURCE (e.g. tooling/). Then drop binary assets + declared sensitive/derived prefixes.
_ledger_self_exclusion: The ledger is excluded from its own coverage on purpose, and this is load-bearing now that research-ledger.jsonl is COMMITTED (and therefore enumerable). Every `record` rewrites it, which changes its hash, which would classify it stale again the instant it was recorded — full coverage would be unreachable by construction and one entry would churn forever. The pretty .json cache is listed too so a checkout that has not yet gitignored it does not count a derived file as source.
_provenance: Keys accepted off an agent RESULT and copied verbatim onto the ledger entry, ON TOP OF ledger-io.mjs's DEFAULT_PROVENANCE_KEYS. This list may only ADD: transport keys (path) and canonical aliases (criticality, what_breaks_if_wrong) are refused no matter what is listed here, because a blind spread of the result is what leaked them next to the canonical whatBreaks in the first place.
